 For high school seniors and their families, fall can feel like the beginning of the college countdown. Applications are underway, college visits are wrapping up, and families are starting to think seriously about how they’ll pay for the next four years.
 For credit unions, this is an important opportunity to step in with something members need just as much as a student loan: clear, timely financial education.
 With the 2027–28 Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) now available, families can begin the financial aid process for students who will attend college next academic year.
 By helping members understand what needs to happen (and when), credit unions can become a trusted resource during one of the biggest financial decisions a family will make.
 The college-prep conversation shouldn't start with the loan
 When families think about paying for college, student loans may be top of mind. But borrowing is only one part of a larger conversation about planning for college costs. Senior year is the right time for students and parents to:
 Finalize their college list and understand application and admission deadlines.
 Complete the FAFSA as soon as possible.
 Research scholarships and grants.
 Review financial aid offers carefully.
 Consider how much the family can contribute out of pocket.
 Understand federal and private borrowing options before deciding how to fill any remaining funding gap.
 Credit unions should offer information to help members navigate these steps before they ever need to apply for a student loan. Include educational articles in newsletters, post tips on social media, host seminars, or attend high school college prep events to position your credit union as a trusted community partner.
 FAFSA season is here ... funding season is coming soon
 The FAFSA is one of the most important steps families can take when preparing to pay for college. Make sure your members know the FAFSA is now available online for students planning to attend school between July 1, 2027, and June 30, 2028, and remind them: Don't just apply to college. Start planning how you'll pay for it.
 College financing can be overwhelming, especially for families navigating it for the first time. Your credit union can guide them with timely, trusted information throughout the process:
 Share FAFSA tips and deadline information.
 Host a college-financing seminar or webinar.
 Partner with local schools and community organizations.
 Connect members with trusted financial aid resources.
 Helping members understand the difference between the total cost of attendance and the amount they’ll need to finance can make the process feel more manageable—and help families make more informed borrowing decisions.
 Give members the resources they need to create a plan for paying for college—and a reason to turn to their credit union when it's time to borrow.
 Highlight the credit union difference
 When it’s time to fill college funding gaps, help members understand the advantages of financing their education through a credit union. Compared to big-bank lenders, credit unions can offer competitive rates, more personalized service, and an education line of credit that provides added flexibility throughout the college planning and borrowing process.
 Unlike a traditional student loan, borrowers can apply for an education line of credit at any time, providing access to funds whenever they are needed for eligible education expenses.
 In some cases, borrowers can even apply before they know which school they’ll attend or exactly how much they’ll need to borrow. Once they’re ready, they can complete the process and draw funds as needed, rather than borrowing the full amount upfront.
 Student Choice can help
 Student Choice offers educational resources to help credit unions support members throughout the college financing journey. Our upcoming FAFSA webinar , led by College Counselor Tricia Poplicean, provides practical guidance on completing the FAFSA and understanding what comes next.
 Contact us  to learn more about our private student lending solutions and educational resources that can help your credit union support members from college planning through financing.
